timeline.event: Rome is founded, according to tradition, by Romulus
timeline.label: c. 753 BCE

timeline.event: Hannibal leads his army and elephants across the Alps
timeline.label: 218 BCE

timeline.event: Julius Caesar is assassinated in the Roman Senate
timeline.label: 44 BCE

timeline.event: Octavian takes the title Augustus, becoming the first Roman emperor
timeline.label: 27 BCE

timeline.event: Mount Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii
timeline.label: 79 CE

timeline.event: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, last emperor in the West
Construction of the Leaning Tower of Pisa begins
Marco Polo sets out from Venice on his journey to China
Brunelleschi's dome of Florence Cathedral is completed
Michelangelo finishes painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling
Pope Gregory XIII introduces the Gregorian calendar
Galileo is put on trial by the Roman Inquisition
The Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed
Mussolini's Fascists stage the March on Rome
The Lateran Treaty creates the independent Vatican City
Italians vote in a referendum to become a republic
The Treaty of Rome founds the European Economic Community
Rome hosts the Summer Olympic Games
Euro notes and coins replace the Italian lira
Italy wins its fourth football World Cup in Berlin

places.name: Rome
places.clue: Fittingly for the Eternal City, it surrounds an entire country: Vatican City, the world's smallest state.

places.name: Venice
places.clue: Built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon, it is stitched together by some 400 bridges.

places.name: Florence
places.clue: Brunelleschi's cathedral dome here is still the largest brick dome ever built.

places.name: Milan
places.clue: Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper is painted on the refectory wall of a convent in this city.

places.name: Pompeii
places.clue: Buried by Vesuvius in 79 CE, this Roman town lay preserved under ash for some 1,500 years before its rediscovery.

places.name: Mount Etna
places.clue: Europe's tallest active volcano erupts so often that its height keeps changing.

places.name: Cinque Terre
places.clue: Five colourful fishing villages cling to these Ligurian cliffs, linked by footpaths and a coastal railway.

places.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
places.clue: These three limestone towers in the Dolomites stood on the front line between Italy and Austria in the First World War.

places.name: Matera
places.clue: Its ancient cave dwellings, the Sassi, were evacuated in the 1950s, yet it became a European Capital of Culture in 2019.

places.name: Aosta
places.clue: Its Roman gate, theatre and walls have earned this Alpine town the nickname 'Rome of the Alps'.

places.name: Lecce
places.clue: Its exuberant Baroque churches, carved from soft golden local stone, earn it the nickname 'Florence of the South'.

places.name: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
places.clue: This Bronze Age stone fortress is the finest surviving example of Sardinia's thousands of cone-shaped nuraghe towers.
